question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}{{f}^{″}({x}_{n})},
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ and ${f}^{″}({x}_{n})$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n},$ respectively.

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =({x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-3x+4)^{′}=3{x}^{2}+2x-3, \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =(3{x}^{2}+2x-3)^{′}=6x+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{3{x}_{n}^{2}+2{x}_{n}-3}{6{x}_{n}+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{3{x}_{0}^{2}+2{x}_{0}-3}{6{x}_{0}+2} \\  & =0-\frac{3(0)^{2}+2(0)-3}{6(0)+2} \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-\frac{3{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}-3}{6{x}_{1}+2} \\  & =1.5-\frac{3(1.5)^{2}+2(1.5)-3}{6(1.5)+2} \\  & ≈0.886,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
